stem:
The diagram shows point $P$, line $L$, and points $F$ and $Q$ on $L$. Segment $PF$ meets $L$ at right angles. Segment $PQ$ is slanted.

Which two claims correctly describe the perpendicular projection of $P$ onto $L$?

options.text: The foot $F$ is the perpendicular projection of $P$ onto $L$.
Call the answer plane only, with no choice between $F$ and $Q$.
$PF$ is shorter than $PQ$ because the perpendicular segment is the shortest path from $P$ to $L$.
Point $Q$ is the projection because $Q$ is the rightmost labelled point on $L$.

teacher.key_rationale: Perpendicular foot F is the projection; PF is shortest to L. Naming only plane skips the foot. Choosing rightmost Q captures a surface label.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote quadrilateral grid into P, F, Q on line L.
